item.title: Anthropic S-1 Reveals Rapid Growth Ahead of Blockbuster IPO
item.description: Ahead of what could be the largest public listing ever, Anthropic said revenue soared to $16.3 billion in the first half of the year, and it planned to spend $807 billion on A.I. infrastructure.

item.title: AI Is Finding a Flood of Bugs, and Silicon Valley Is Rushing to Fix Them
item.description: A.I. has uncovered a horde of software flaws, which engineers are racing to fix before they can be exploited and abused by hackers.

item.title: GM Is Leaving NYSE for the Nasdaq After More Than 100 Years
item.description: After more than 100 years on the New York Stock Exchange, the automaker is shifting its listing to the Nasdaq, which is home to many technology companies.

item.media:description: At a General Motors factory in Tennessee.

item.title: In the A.I. ‘Robogym,’ Machines Train to Be More Like Humans

item.title: The Key Numbers From Anthropic’s IPO Filing
item.description: We broke down the A.I. company’s key figures, which give insight into the health of its business, its future plans and who’s in charge.
item.dc:creator: Sri Muppidi and Lauren Hirsch
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Anthropic’s Code W/ Claude event in San Francisco in May. In a filing, the company provided rare insight into the business of a “frontier” A.I. lab that makes cutting-edge A.I. models.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO S-1 Spells Out a Future of Promise and Peril
item.description: The A.I. company took great pains to describe the many benefits that can come from using its Claude chatbot and technology, but also offered up a heavy dose of gloom.
item.dc:creator: Mike Isaac

item.title: Meet Anthropic’s Seven Founders as the A.I. Firm Prepares for an IPO
item.description: Former OpenAI employees started the company in 2021 after disagreements over how to safely build artificial intelligence. An I.P.O. could make them billionaires.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin

item.title: Darline Graham Gets Help From the Data Center Industry in South Carolina Senate Race
item.description: As political fights over artificial intelligence accelerate, there is now a super PAC aligned with the data center industry. Its first bet is on Ms. Graham, a Republican in an unexpectedly tight race.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer and Emily Davies
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham of South Carolina has been friendlier toward the data center industry than her Democratic opponent, trying to walk a line between backing the centers’ development as a national security necessity while stressing the need for community involvement.

item.title: What’s Riding on Anthropic Going Public? Nearly Everything.
item.description: Anthropic sits atop a pyramid of business partners and suppliers, making it a barometer of the broader economy. Its initial public offering will have widespread implications.
item.dc:creator: Erin Griffith and Lauren Hirsch

item.title: Put Your A.I. Agents to Work with These 5 Killer Tasks
item.description: When you start using Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s dots for these tasks — like applying for jobs and booking hard-to-get restaurant tables — you may never go back.
item.dc:creator: Brian X. Chen

item.title: Elon Musk Says Ukraine Violated Starlink’s Rules
item.description: The comments came after the disruption in the country’s satellite service. Earlier, Ukraine said drones using Starshield, the Pentagon-funded service, were back to normal speeds.
item.dc:creator: Sheera Frenkel, Siobhán O’Grady and Liubov Sholudko
item.media:credit: Lynsey Addario for The New York Times
item.media:description: Ukrainian soldiers operated a drone over Russian-occupied territory from the Zaporizhzhia region in 2023.

item.title: Why Anger About Data Centers and Energy Prices May Not Swing Votes
item.description: In Ohio, many voters say their frustration about the increase in electricity and fuel prices and the growth of data centers won’t influence whom they vote for.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott and Maddie McGarvey
item.media:description: In interviews, Ohio residents described data centers as threats to their communities. But many of them said the issue was not driving their choice for senator or governor.

item.title: What Is PHP? Why Are Government and Business Websites Going Offline?
item.description: A critical security flaw in the programming language underpinning much of the web has prompted a global rush to patch vulnerable systems.
item.dc:creator: Karla Adam and Dustin Volz
item.media:description: A programmer in Guernica, Spain, on Thursday, working on PHP code, software used throughout the internet.

item.title: How a Legal Backlash Against Big Tech Is Forcing Big Changes
item.description: A series of lawsuits has created a new de facto regulatory regime as courts order companies like Meta and Google to change their business practices — and pay up.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang
item.media:description: Meta’s chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg. On Wednesday, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a record $25 billion penalty for abusing consumer privacy.

item.title: PHP Security Flaw Sets Off Global Rush to Patch, Leaving Websites Offline
item.description: Governments and businesses around the world scrambled to prevent hackers from exploiting a vulnerability in PHP, a popular programming language.
item.dc:creator: Lynsey Chutel, Amelia Nierenberg and Brian O. Otieno
item.media:description: Prime Minister Rob Jetten of the Netherlands in Brussels last week. He said that his cabinet was closely monitoring the online vulnerability caused by a security flaw in PHP.

item.title: How the A.I. Boom Is Driving Up Sales of Gray Paint
item.description: Tech companies are painting data centers with gray coatings on top of gray concrete and steel to resist fire, rust and static electricity. That has made data centers a fast-growing market for paint makers.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin

item.title: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California’s Proposed Wealth Tax
item.description: The billionaire told Meta’s board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for sale. The company remade its stock structure to help him pay the tax if voters pass it.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Victor Llorente for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mark Zuckerberg, the chief executive of Meta, at his home in Lake Tahoe, Calif. He has another California home in Palo Alto, close to Meta’s headquarters.

item.title: Anthropic Joins the A.I. Agent Race With Claude Duet
item.description: The tool, which is not yet widely available, will compete with OpenAI’s dots and Meta’s Muse. It is built for work and not personal errands.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:description: Anthropic’s new A.I. agent, Claude Duet.

item.title: Meta Earnings Show Increased A.I. Spending, Even as Cash Pressures Grow
item.description: The spending has hurt the Silicon Valley giant’s cash flow, which turned negative. Meta said it would issue a new class of stock to help it raise more money.

item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing
item.media:description: A General Motors factory for electric vehicles in Lake Orion, Mich. The company said this week that it would drastically cut the cost of electric vehicle batteries.

item.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion Over Cambridge Analytica Privacy Violations
item.description: The penalty, one of the largest levied against a tech giant, stemmed from a lawsuit by New Mexico claiming the social media company had misled users about their data privacy.
